newsitem.title: CHINA: China expands local currency interbank market.
newsitem.headline: China expands local currency interbank market.

text.p: China has expanded its local currency interbank market, admitting dozens of urban cooperative banks in major Chinese cities as first-tier trading members, the Shanghai Securities News said on Monday.
The move extended the market's first-tier trading, which had previously been restricted to the provincial level, to major cities, the newspaper said.
The market now had 89 first-tier members able to directly borrow and lend short-term funds through the exchange's computerised trading system, the newspaper said.
First-tier members include state banks, city cooperative banks and short-term financial centres which are money brokerages run by the central bank.

The market also has hundreds of second-tier members which trade through the short-term finance centres and include major Chinese securities brokerages, trust firms and financial companies associated with major industrial groups as well as a number of designated foreign banks.
The market was established in January 1996 to enable banks and non-banking financial institutions to trade short-term funds within 120 days amongst themselves.
Beijing's ultimate aim was to make the market a barometer of China's short term money supply, traders said.
The market's major problem was that it was too small to effectively reflect China's short-term money movements, they said.
The market has had an average daily turnover of around 2.5 billion yuan since its set-up, only a fraction of China's securities trading volume in the same period.
